writeup.p: Per-slot equipment sync for tracked entities. EntityTrackerEntry pushes it when a tracked entity's equipment changes (line ~399 in the bundled sources) and EntityLivingBase broadcasts it on item or armor updates (line ~1644). The payload is the entity id, a short slot 0-4 (0 held item, 1-4 boots/legs/chest/helmet) and a Slot-encoded ItemStack that may be null to clear. The initial burst arrives at entity spawn so the client can render held items and armor before other entity data matters.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityEquipment resolves the entity and calls setCurrentItemOrArmor(slot, item), which writes into the EntityLivingBase equipment array that the render layers read every frame. The local player is exempt: the client's own equipment never arrives as S04, it is driven by inventory and held-item packets, so this channel is strictly about other entities.

The corpus yields two non-vanilla references, both dead imports: Rise 5.99 Aura.java imports S04 at line 43 and never uses it in the body, and Sigma 4.11 InventoryManager.java imports it at line 30 while actually processing S09PacketHeldItemChange and S1CPacketEntityMetadata. Rise 6.1.30/6.2.4 expose it only through the script API whitelist (NetworkAPI.java line 50). No ESP, tracer, nametag or AntiBot module hooks it, because those features read the equipment array the vanilla handler already updated: intercepting the packet would duplicate state the client already owns.

None in the corpus. The packet is server-authored and the client has no serverbound equipment channel to abuse. The theoretical value is weapon-switch intelligence: slot-0 S04 deltas reveal exactly when a tracked opponent swaps tools, which is timing data a combat module could use, but none of the 8 clients implements it. Anti-cheats do not police the packet because the client cannot influence it.

overview: Equipment sync for tracked entities that the vanilla handler commits straight into EntityLivingBase, which is why every armor-aware feature in the 8 clients reads the fields instead of the packet. The only non-vanilla references are two dead imports (Rise 5.99 Aura, Sigma 4.11 InventoryManager) and the Rise 6.x script whitelist; no module processes it, so the module list is empty by corpus fact, not by omission.
server_handling: The server-side senders are EntityTrackerEntry (on tracked-equipment change, line ~399) and EntityLivingBase (on item/armor updates, line ~1644). There is no serverbound counterpart: the client reports inventory changes through C09PacketHeldItemChange and C0EPacketClickWindow, and the server echoes the resulting equipment state to other trackers as S04. Nothing in the server validates the packet because it never receives it.
protocol_notes: Fields in order: VarInt entity id, short slot, then a Slot-encoded ItemStack (short item id + count + damage + optional NBT, with id -1 encoding null). One packet per slot, so a full armor change is five packets; the client applies them independently and a late packet can overwrite a newer value if ordering slips, which is a known quirk of the 1.8 entity-equipment path.
anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures this packet: it is clientbound, server-authored and carries no timing or movement signal. The only consumer-side risk would be a module that uses slot-0 deltas to time attacks, which would inherit whatever the target's anti-cheat flags for reaction-time consistency; nothing in the corpus does this.
client_variations: The only client-side deltas are the dead imports (Rise 5.99 Aura, Sigma 4.11 InventoryManager) and the Rise 6.x script API entry; everything else in all 8 clients is the untouched vanilla handler.
